options: Hello, World! Java was released in 1995 (one line)
Hello, World! and Java was released in 1995 on two lines
quiz.explain: Each println ends its line, so the output is two lines. "Java was released in " + 1995 glues the number onto the text.

options: This line, because Java is case-sensitive
It compiles, but fails when you run it
quiz.explain: It must be System with a capital S. With a small s, javac looks for a package called system and stops.

quiz.q: Is this a valid Java 25 program (Hello.java)?
options: No, every program needs public class
Yes, it is a compact source file (JEP 512, final in Java 25)
quiz.explain: Since Java 25 a compact source file is a full program; the compiler adds an implicit class. In Java 23 this was a preview (JEP 477).

quiz.q: What does javac produce from HelloWorld.java?
quiz.explain: javac compiles to bytecode. The JVM then interprets that bytecode or JIT-compiles it to machine code when the program runs.

quiz.q: What does Write Once, Run Anywhere mean?
options: Java needs no installation at all
The same bytecode runs on every system that has a JVM
You must recompile for every operating system
Java only runs in the browser
quiz.explain: The bytecode is the same on Windows, macOS and Linux; each computer still needs a JVM (from a JDK or JRE) to run it.

quiz.q: Who frees memory that a Java program no longer uses?
options: The operating system after each line
quiz.explain: Java has automatic memory management: the garbage collector removes objects the program no longer uses.

options: Two different languages with similar names
Java is the old name of JavaScript
quiz.explain: They are different languages. JavaScript runs mainly in the browser; Java runs on the JVM.

quiz.q: Which statement about Java 23 and Java 25 is correct?
options: Java 23 is long-term support, Java 25 is short-term
Java 25 is long-term support; Java 23 was a short-term release
quiz.explain: Java 23 (September 2024) was replaced by Java 24 in March 2025. Java 25 (September 2025) is an LTS release. System.out.println works in both.

quiz.q: Who designed Java, and when was it released?
options: James Gosling's team at Sun Microsystems, 1995
quiz.explain: James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems released Java in 1995. Oracle has owned it since 2010.

flashcards.front: What kind of language is Java?
flashcards.back: A high-level, class-based, object-oriented language. All code lives inside a class.
James Gosling's team at Sun Microsystems, released in 1995. Oracle has owned it since 2010.
It compiles a .java file into bytecode: a .class file.
It runs bytecode: it interprets it or JIT-compiles it to machine code.

flashcards.front: What is Write Once, Run Anywhere?
flashcards.back: The same bytecode runs on any system with a JVM, without recompiling.

flashcards.front: Does Write Once, Run Anywhere mean no installation?
flashcards.back: No. The computer still needs a JVM, from a JDK or JRE.

flashcards.front: What does the garbage collector do?
flashcards.back: It removes objects the program no longer uses: automatic memory management.

flashcards.front: What does Java leave out compared with C++?
flashcards.back: Pointers, manual memory management and multiple inheritance of classes.

flashcards.front: Where does a Java program start running?

flashcards.back: Different languages. JavaScript runs mainly in the browser; Java runs on the JVM.

flashcards.front: system.out.println vs Main instead of main?
flashcards.back: system.out does not compile. Main compiles, but java stops with Main method not found.
Java 23 was short-term (replaced in March 2025). Java 25 (September 2025) is LTS.

flashcards.back: JDK 23 with the classic style, so the checks pass. JDK 25 for jshell and Gym Log.
